Funding News

ReplyAll raises Rs 9.7 crore in funding

Wear brand ReplyAll has raised Rs 9.7 crore in a funding round led by Sadev Ventures and Atom XVII. The round also saw participation from ISV, represented by Jivraj Singh Sachar, and Long View Ventures, alongside continued participation from existing investors Sparrow and Antler, and a group of angel investors.

The capital will support fabric research and development, product design, new categories, and the brand's retail and community presence.

Founded by Rushabh Sanghavi in 2025, ReplyAll is building everyday performance wear for

people whose lives move between work, travel, sport and everything in between. 

Bucketlistt raises seed round led by Kairon Capital

Bucketlistt.com has raised Rs. 7.6 crore in a seed round led by Kairon Capital, with participation from Titan Capital, Divisa Family Office and Kunal Popat. Bucketlistt.com helps travellers discover and book verified travel experiences. 

The company, launched in Rishikesh in December 2025, is used to manage bookings, inventory, agents, payments and daily operations. The company was founded in 2025 by Shubham Makhecha (CA - All India Rank 36, ex-Accenture and PwC), Nitant Desai (CA, ex-PwC, trek leader) and Divyam Shah, a full-stack developer who leads technology. 

Other News

Swiggy renews insurance policy for its delivery partners

Swiggy has announced the renewal of its insurance programme for delivery partners with IndusInd General Insurance Company Ltd (formerly known as Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd). 

In FY26, more than 25 lakh delivery partners were covered under Swiggy's accident and health insurance programmes, said the company. 


Under the renewed insurance programme with IndusInd General Insurance, delivery partners will continue to receive accidental death cover of Rs 10,00,000, in-patient hospitalization cover of up to Rs 2,00,000, and family health coverage up to Rs 1,00,000. 


Additionally, maternity benefits are covered for all women delivery partners and the spouses of male delivery partners wherever family cover is applicable. During the previous policy period, 75% of maternity claims were availed by the spouses of delivery partners, while the remaining 25% were utilized by Swiggy's women delivery partners.

Wow! Momo enters Sri Lanka, eyes UAE and US for QSR expansion

Wow! Momo Foods will begin operations in Sri Lanka by the end of this year, while Wow! FMCG, which has already taken the Wow! brand into 14 countries, has identified the USA, Malaysia, Australia, Thailand and Canada as markets for the next 12 months.


The Sri Lanka launch is led by Softlogic Corporation, a diversified Sri Lankan conglomerate with interests across healthcare, insurance, hospitality and retail, which Wow! Momo Foods has partnered with as its master franchisee.

CheQ appoints Rupal Rajal as Head of Human Resources

CheQ has appointed Rupal Rajal as Head of Human Resources (HR). With over 14 years of experience across fintech, technology, artificial intelligence (AI), Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), consulting and FMCG, Rupal brings extensive experience in building people functions, scaling organisations and aligning human resources strategies with business priorities.

Rupal joins CheQ at a pivotal stage in the company’s growth as it continues to expand its presence across the consumer credit ecosystem. Having evolved from a credit card bill payment and rewards platform into a broader credit ecosystem spanning credit management, credit health insights, utility bill payments, AI-powered credit assistance through Wisor, lending solutions and UPI payments, CheQ is focused on strengthening its capabilities and delivering greater value to consumers.

Ingram Micro India has appointed Farhana Haque as Country Lead & Executive Director, Platform Business, effective 21 October 2026.

item.title: Meta Business Agent aims to turn WhatsApp into a 24/7 storefront for D2C brands
item.description: At TechSparks 2026, Meta’s Piyush Vaidya outlined how Meta Business Agent could help D2C brands use WhatsApp for personalised customer engagement, product discovery and round-the-clock support.
item.content:encoded:
A customer browsing a brand’s Instagram page late at night may have questions about a product, need help choosing the right option or want to know when an order will arrive.

If the business cannot respond immediately, that moment of interest could turn into a lost sale.

For direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, the challenge is not just attracting customers but staying available when they are ready to engage. Meta wants to address this through AI-powered conversations on WhatsApp, turning the messaging platform into a storefront that remains open beyond business hours.

At TechSparks 2026, Piyush Vaidya, Enterprise Sales Specialist for India at Meta, presented Meta Business Agent, a tool designed to help businesses answer customer queries, recommend products and guide shoppers through their purchase journey.

The proposition is to bring product discovery, customer support and commerce closer together, without requiring customers to move between multiple platforms.

From customer queries to conversions

Retailers face several obstacles along the path to purchase, including cart abandonment, limited personalisation, uncertainty about products and the cost of customer support. Vaidya said Meta’s research found that 91% of users drop off after adding products to their carts.

Meta Business Agent aims to reduce this friction by allowing customers to ask questions and explore products through WhatsApp conversations. Businesses can connect their product catalogues and provide instructions that guide how the agent responds. For more complicated queries, the conversation can be handed over to a human representative.

The agent can also retain conversational context, helping businesses offer more relevant responses when customers return. Rather than repeating their requirements, shoppers can continue where an earlier interaction left off.

Businesses remain in control of how the agent operates. They can set its tone, define the topics it handles and choose between manual replies, AI-generated suggestions and automated responses. This gives brands room to introduce automation while keeping customer interactions aligned with their communication style.

Making WhatsApp a shopping destination

Meta is also working to help customers discover businesses directly through WhatsApp. Vaidya outlined entry points such as business contact cards shared in chats, calls to action on WhatsApp Status ads and a search experience intended to make AI-enabled businesses easier to find.

Once customers enter a conversation, businesses can showcase catalogue items, capture leads through forms and facilitate appointment bookings. Piyush Vaidya said payments within WhatsApp are live in India and Brazil, potentially allowing customers to complete more of the purchase journey without leaving the platform.

Businesses can also configure the agent to follow up with shoppers who abandon a purchase, using reminders or relevant product updates to encourage them to return.

Piyush cited Prime Pix Accessories as an example of a small business that reported threefold revenue growth after enabling Meta Business Agent, alongside 30 to 40 daily orders and round-the-clock responses. The presentation did not provide further details on the period or methodology behind the reported growth.

Scaling without losing the human touch

Automation does not mean removing people from customer service. Businesses can test and refine the agent’s responses before customers interact with it, set limits on what it can handle and transfer complex conversations to human staff.

As Piyush Vaidya put it, “You decide when the AI works and who it talks to.”

He said one million businesses had adopted Meta Business Agent at the time of the presentation, with further adoption expected among larger enterprises and businesses using WhatsApp’s business platform.

For D2C brands, the opportunity lies in making customer engagement less dependent on operating hours. If shoppers can discover products, get answers and move towards a purchase in the same conversation, WhatsApp could become both a sales channel and a support layer.

The test will be whether these AI-powered interactions can deliver the personalisation and reliability customers expect while earning the trust needed to turn conversations into lasting relationships.

item.title: Paytm sees 10x rise in net profit in Q2 of FY27
item.description: The revenue of company for the second quarter of FY27 stood at Rs 2,648 crore which was an annual growth of 28.4%.
item.content:encoded:
Paytm reported a net profit of Rs 225 crore for the second quarter of FY27 which was almost a 10x rise when compared to Rs 21 crore recorded in the similar period of last fiscal.

The revenue for the second quarter came in at Rs 2,648 crore as compared to Rs 2,061 crore registered in the similar period of last fiscal, recording a year-on-year (YoY) growth of 28.4%.

According to the company, the EBITDA rose 90% on a year-on-year basis with the EBITDA margin expanding to 10%. Paytm said distribution of financial services revenue grew 49% YoY to Rs 912 crore, with key financial services customers increasing 35% YoY to 8.8 lakh. The net payment revenue increased 21% YoY on a comparable basis to Rs 644 crore.

According to Paytm, with a focus on monetisable user base, it gained consumer UPI payment market share for the sixth consecutive quarter, with Paytm UPI GTV growing at more than double the industry growth rate. Monthly transacting users increased by 1 crore YoY to 8.5 crore, the highest addition in nearly three years, driven by better product, stronger acquisition and retention, and AI-led personalisation.

Paytm said AI is increasingly becoming the operating system with fine-tuned models and agents deployed across consumer, merchant and engineering journeys, risk management, collections, fraud prevention and personalisation. AI-led efficiencies helped reduce indirect expenses as a share of revenue to 46% from 52% a year ago. The company has also begun offering its AI platform to enterprise merchants, extending its in-house capabilities to help them grow and engage customers across channels.

Paytm said with a large addressable market, accelerating revenue growth and AI-led improvements in structural operating leverage, it expects sustained revenue growth and margin expansion to drive long-term profit growth.

item.title: Ather Energy swings to Rs 1.26 Cr profit in Q2
item.description: Ather Energy swung to a consolidated net profit in Q2 FY27 as revenue from operations grew 63% year-on-year. The electric two-wheeler maker plans to expand production capacity to meet rising demand.
item.content:encoded:
Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1.26 crore in the second quarter of FY27, reversing a net loss of Rs 154 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Revenue from operations rose 63% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 1,464.24 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 898.88 crore a year earlier. Total income, including other income, increased 62% to Rs 1,526.95 crore.

The company sold 93,211 electric two-wheelers during the quarter, up 42% YoY. Its operating performance improved alongside the growth in sales, with the company reporting a positive EBITDA for the quarter.

Ather's consolidated adjusted gross margin improved 160 basis points YoY to 24%, despite higher input costs for aluminium, copper, lithium and crude-linked plastics. The company attributed the improvement to product mix and pricing decisions.

Non-vehicle revenue, which includes subscriptions, charging, accessories, spares and services, accounted for 15% of revenue from operations, up from 12% a year earlier. Ather also said 94% of its customers opted for AtherStack Pro.

Demand continued to outpace production capacity, with enquiries rising 109% YoY to around 10 lakh and pre-orders more than doubling to 1.8 lakh. The company's Hosur facility in Tamil Nadu operated at 98% capacity utilisation during peak production.

To support demand, Ather plans to increase annual production capacity at Hosur by 75,000 units to 4.95 lakh units by December 2026. Its upcoming facility at AURIC in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, is expected to begin phased commercial production from December 2026, with an initial annual capacity of five lakh units.

The company plans to add another 1.5 lakh units of annual capacity at the new facility by Q2 FY28. Once the expansion is completed, its combined installed capacity across the two facilities is expected to reach around 11.4 lakh units. Ather's board has approved capital expenditure of up to Rs 122 crore for the expansion.

During the quarter, Ather launched Konarc, its first scooter built on the new EL platform, at its Community Day event on August 29. It also introduced Ather TrueHealth, a vehicle health report that estimates resale value, and AtherNode, a charging solution for apartment complexes.

Tarun Mehta, Co-founder & CEO, Ather Energy, said, “We delivered a strong quarter, with robust topline growth and a positive bottomline, despite surging commodity prices and supply chain disruptions."

"Underpinning this is a shift to electric two-wheelers that is now structural and playing out across India. At Ather, demand has more than doubled year-on-year this quarter, and to meet it, we are further augmenting our production capacity at Hosur and AURIC. With Konarc taking Ather to a wider set of customers, we see significant headroom for growth ahead."
